description:
Tier 2 and probably the highest-value rewrite here. Argon2 is memory-hard: it fills a 64 KiB to 1 GiB block array with a BLAKE2b-based mixing function and makes data-dependent (argon2i: independent) passes over it; the reference (phc-winner-argon2) is plain C with optional SSE, and argon2_elixir wraps it with dirty schedulers because a hash takes 10-500 ms. A kernel of the same code yields every 250 us, is killed cleanly with its memory freed when the process dies, and is bounds-checked. The memory is one alloc'd [i64] of m_cost KiB (well under the 2^48 cap).

Kernel: `argon2id(password :: [u8], salt :: [u8], t_cost :: i64, m_cost_kib :: i64, parallelism :: i64, out_len :: i64) :: [u8]` with lanes computed sequentially (parallelism > 1 changes the indexing, not the result; a multi-process version can split lanes across kernel calls later), BLAKE2b from the sibling ticket inlined (or its long-hash variant H'), the G mixing function over 1 KiB blocks (u64 wrapping adds and rotates), and the index computation for argon2id's hybrid mode. Vectors from the RFC 9106 test cases and argon2_elixir's own outputs.

Elixir baseline: there is none (nobody hashes passwords in pure Elixir); the comparison is argon2_elixir itself (reference C), so the verdict is about parity and the runtime contract, not a speedup. Pre-register: expected marginal on speed, with tick-gap and process-kill measurements beside it.

Governance, stated in the header: a password-hashing implementation needs review before any production use; the kernel's test vectors and agreement give correctness, not an audit; constant-time behaviour is not required for argon2id's data-independent first half but the final comparison must happen in Elixir with a constant-time compare (:crypto.hash_equals/2).

Needs: defk-w38, defk-n4r.2, defk-ivt, defk-n4r.4, the BLAKE2b ticket, big alloc (works today), rotates (the builtins ticket).

Done when: RFC 9106 vectors pass, output matches argon2_elixir for random parameters within the supported ranges, the kill-mid-hash test shows frames_live back to 0 and memory released, verdict and tick gap recorded.

comments.text: Done: examples/argon2.exs (merged main at 8816a0e). Verdict vs argon2_elixir 4.1.3 (reference ref.c, dirty CPU, lanes on pthreads), provisional under load (load 14-40, M4 Pro): POOR at argon2_elixir's defaults (t=3, 64 MiB, 4 lanes): 19.5-24.4 vs 75-90 ms, 0.25-0.29x, because the C runs 4 lanes on 4 threads and the kernel computes lanes in sequence (256 MiB, 4 lanes: 0.23-0.29x). Lane for lane LEVEL with the reference C: 0.88-0.95x at t=1/1 MiB, 0.91-1.05x at t=2/16 MiB (OWASP minimum rounded; second DEFK_RESULT line argon2_one_lane, accepted as marginal or poor), 0.92-0.98x at t=3/64 MiB. Pre-registered 'marginal on speed' held for one lane only. 24 concurrent hashes at defaults: 235-285 vs 275-589 ms. Tick gap (1 ms ticker, one scheduler): idle floor 2.0-2.5 ms, argon2_elixir 2.0-2.1 (dirty, never holds a normal scheduler), kernel 2.2-2.5; 5-9 ms outliers both sides under load. Kill mid-hash (t=4, 256 MiB, killed at 60 ms): kernel frames_live 1 -> 0 and :erlang.memory(:binary) +256 MiB -> +0 at once; argon2_elixir's process dies at once but the C runs on, holding its dirty scheduler and ~135-150 MiB: a probe hash with 1 dirty scheduler online waited 403-498 ms. Correctness: RFC 9106 5.1-5.3 (d, i, id with secret+AD) pass; 60 random parameter sets equal argon2_elixir (all types); 40 argon2id sets with arbitrary m equal phc-winner-argon2's CLI built from argon2_elixir's vendored sources; forced yields; bad params raise in both modes; Elixir mode equals the kernel (small sizes + RFC vectors). Governance in header; verify uses :crypto.hash_equals/2. No pure-BEAM argon2 on Hex; jargon 1.1.0 rejected as oracle (ARGON2_VERSION 13 decimal, not 0x13). New tickets: defk-3z5 (write-not-returned false positive when a param is written then rebound and returned), defk-52v.17 (lane parallelism needs disjoint writes to one array; value semantics copies per slice). Code size data point on defk-6ag. performance.md 6.19, 6.20, 7.7, 7.8; README row under 'Where Elixir is the right choice'.

title: argon2id from scratch vs argon2_elixir, with the yield and memory story
